On 2027-02-20 04:18 PM PST Emma Johnson wrote:
> Can Redwood provide one short example of how the tokenization flow would look for a name/SSN (pseudonymization example)?

Hi Emma — quick technical notes to address that:

- Redwood processing model: we can be configured for ephemeral processing (no long-term storage of raw inputs) or for customer-requested short-term retention to support debugging. For PHI-sensitive customers the standard is: ephemeral processing + KMS-backed access logging.
- Tokenization/pseudonymization example (simple flow):
  1) Input arrives at inference endpoint -> field-level parser extracts candidate PHI fields (name, ssn).
  2) Fields are hashed + salted with customer-specific KMS key (one-way token) before entering model pipeline.
  3) Model runs on tokenized inputs; raw input never written to long-term storage.
  4) Audit logs record token id + request metadata (timestamp, model, route) — logs can be exported in CSV/JSON.
- Logs retention: default staging retention is 90 days; we can configure shorter/longer windows per contract.
- Evidence we can supply: sample sanitized log export (JSON), encryption key policy summary, and a short runbook for incident response.

I can bring sample tokenization pseudocode and a sanitized log export to the walkthrough. If you prefer, I can draft a 1-page illustration for Emma/legal showing the exact fields we would redact vs hash.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Principal Applied ML Engineer | Redwood Inference
